target_customer: Startups and tech companies buying commercial insurance, later expanded to other industries and brokers
problem: Startups buy insurance through brokers with slow, opaque underwriting and high fees.
business_model: Full stack insurance carrier earning premiums, plus claims administration, financial products and ETFs

founders.name: Nico Laqua
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no employers or education.

founders.name: Emily Yuan
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no employers or education.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a licensed carrier with underwriting, claims and compliance as a small team is regulatory and engineering heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier licenses and admitted status are hard to obtain, but startup insurance products themselves are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; startup insurance brokers continue to operate alongside Corgi.

market_need_then: Startups bought D&O, cyber and E&O through brokers; no dated source on complaints or spend was opened.

branding.domain_note: Bought corgi.com in March 2026 to consolidate products, per FinTech Global.

identity.mascot_or_character: Trudy, a real corgi who appears around the office and a public cafe in San Francisco

branding.community_and_virality: Press mentions of the office dog and cafe; no merch or fan accounts confirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly animal name carried by a real mascot, and the CEO called the corgi.com purchase a step toward a global brand; effect on growth not measured.

outcome_analysis: Corgi reported $108M in January 2026 at a $630M valuation and a $160M Series B at $1.3B in May 2026, then reportedly another round at a higher valuation, and its site claims over $450M raised. The pace of raising and a 250 person team show very fast execution, though outlets disagree on later valuations and the long term insurance risk is untested.
notes: The January 2026 round is described as combined seed and Series A, so stage is other. Lead differs by outlet (Kindred versus co-led with YC). A May 28 2026 round of about $106M at $2.6B (one outlet headlines $40.7M) and a $500K September 2024 seed were seen only in aggregators or conflicting snippets, so they are not recorded as rounds. Company site claims over $450M raised, unverified by a second source. Competitor sources found were 2026 comparison pages, so the dated list is empty.
